static_traits.name: Li Yan
static_traits.family_status: Mother was a nurse; other details not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Estranged from colleagues, little communication; has one good friend, but has not yet confided work troubles to them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Fairly cooperative, positive attitude; clear expression, acceptable organization; tense emotions, anxiety, often using self-deprecating expressions and extreme wording

basic_info.main_problem: I always feel useless because I always spill some customer's coffee when serving at the cafe. This makes me feel incompetent with low self-worth; the problem started 6 months ago when I began working at the cafe, especially noticeable during busy hours, and causes me to feel anxious and doubt my abilities every time before work.
basic_info.core_demands: Anxiety and self-doubt that keep intensifying before work prompted me to seek counseling, hoping to cope with and manage these feelings.
growth_experiences: Started working at the cafe about 6 months ago, needing to manage multiple tables and orders simultaneously; during busy hours frequently interpreting mistakes (e.g. spilling coffee, order errors) as 'I am useless', followed by anxiety, disturbed sleep, estrangement from colleagues and other changes. This work experience significantly triggered and reinforced negative evaluations of self-ability.

special_situations.event: During the cafe's peak hours, multiple tables of customers and multiple orders need to be handled simultaneously, and coffee spills or order errors occur
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make any mistake at work, it proves I am incompetent and should not stay here
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-focuses on details and repeatedly self-checks, trying to do everything perfectly to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I messed up again, I am unworthy of working here

special_situations.event: Before each shift, imagines in advance situations of making mistakes or being complained about
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as one mistake occurs, the consequences will be very bad (customer complaints, manager blame, even being fired)
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly rehearses procedures in advance, worries excessively, and stays highly vigilant to 'prevent mistakes'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Something will definitely go wrong today; I will surely mess up

special_situations.event: Customers or colleagues give positive feedback (for example a customer praises 'this is the best latte')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only long-term, completely impeccable performance counts as truly capable; occasional good performance does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or weakening positive evidence, continuing to demand of oneself with strict standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is just luck, it does not mean I am really good

special_situations.event: Daily interaction with colleagues or work scenes where one is noticed by colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others notice my mistakes, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding communication with colleagues, minimizing socializing to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am incompetent

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen as capable and able to perform the job stably
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as incompetent and thus rejected, looked down upon by peers or losing work
defense_goal: Reducing opportunities to expose mistakes through self-monitoring and avoidance
Preemptively self-deprecating to reduce the blow of others' negation

object_relations.object_representation: Others who are critical and ready to blame at any time (customers/colleagues/managers)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites one to review successful experiences or accept positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing positive evidence to chance or external factors, worrying about being expected more because of it, tending to negate its value
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying positive feedback, emphasizing 'just luck / does not mean anything'; reserved tone, slightly unconfident, avoiding lingering on positive details.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests communicating with colleagues or seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding seeking help as troubling others or exposing incompetence, thus turning to reproach oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using expressions like 'I can just endure it myself / should not trouble others', lowering voice and avoiding eye contact, quickly ending the topic.

manifestations: Distant from colleagues, deliberately reducing communication
Having close friends but not yet sharing work troubles, fearing being looked down upon
outcomes: Worsened anxiety before and during work
Decreased sense of self-worth and self-doubt

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believing colleagues will look down on oneself, seeing oneself as incompetent, thus avoiding contact with colleagues
Presets others' negative evaluations in interaction scenes, leading to more tension

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Continuously self-scrutinizing and self-blaming before and during work, trying to avoid mistakes through perfection
When busy, is overly cautious and careful; hard to respond flexibly

exception_events.target_problem: During cafe busy hours, the client usually anticipates disaster, becoming highly tense and making mistakes (e.g. spilling coffee), then engaging in self-denial and estranging from colleagues.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During one busy shift, the client did not yet keep making mistakes as before, but completed the shift's tasks relatively steadily, with no major problems yet, feeling more in control subjectively.
exception_events.reason: Clue: at the time the task rhythm matched their own state, focus was higher; possibly more familiar with the process, thereby reducing tension and error rate.

exception_events.target_problem: When mistakes occur or are anticipated (e.g. spilling coffee), the client usually immediately attributes them to being 'useless', ignoring positive performance, and anxiety escalates.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, when making coffee for a customer, the customer gave positive feedback of 'the best-tasting latte'; the performance that time was recognized, and the client briefly felt they had 'done it right'.
exception_events.reason: Clue: at that time they were more engaged in the production steps and gained immediate external affirmation, which enhanced the sense of competence and the presentness of attention.

positive_force: Having received positive customer feedback (possessing verifiable work-skill fragments)
Also has experience of stably completing shift tasks under high-pressure situations
Willing to seek help and accept cognitive restructuring (good motivation and cooperation)
Potential support resources exist (has one close friend)
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mind reading and negating the positive
Self-worth strongly bound to single performances, prone to falling into 'all-or-nothing' self-labeling
Multi-tasking and fast pace in work situations bring sustained pressure load
Disturbed sleep, reducing emotion regulation and attention control
Avoids communication with colleagues, reducing opportunities for support and feedback correction

target_behavior.behavior: Work-related anticipatory and situational anxiety (faster heart rate, tension, repeated worry about mistakes)
antecedent: Situations requiring handling multiple tables and multiple orders at once
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly binding a single mistake to overall self-worth, and catastrophically predicting the consequences (being complained about, blamed, or fired)
target_behavior.function: Escapes evaluation and potential failure, seeks a sense of control through hypervigilance
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep disturbance, scattered attention and impaired performance, increased likelihood of mistakes, estrangement from colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-labeling and self-denial (e.g. 'I am useless', 'I always mess up')
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralization and black-and-white thinking, ignoring positive evidence
target_behavior.function: Reducing the impact of external criticism and expectation gaps through preemptive self-blame (self-protection)
target_behavior.consequence: Lowered self-esteem, intensified anxiety, further avoiding socializing and cooperation, affecting work performance
